boundary: This proves a nonzero and multi-million lower bound, not the final global U6 singleton coefficient. The 63 witnesses came from a deterministic sample; additional singleton orbits certainly may exist. A complete orbit or distributed syndrome census is still required for equality.

singleton_verifier.method: For target syndrome s, enumerate all C(240,3) triples; every weight-six representative splits into two disjoint triples, so a complementary triple-syndrome lookup exhausts the fiber. Binary search in the complete weight-four image excludes the entire lower shadow.

theorem: The global U6 lower shadow is closed exactly, and singleton weight-six fibers are proved to exist in abundance. All 134,839,021 errors of weights 0,2,4 map to exactly 91,007,752 syndromes; every weight-0 or weight-2 syndrome already occurs at weight 4, so the lower-shadow image equals the weight-four image. An exact triple-pair fiber verifier then certifies 63 explicit weight-six errors whose syndromes are absent from that lower shadow and have no second weight-six representative. These witnesses lie in 63 disjoint regular PGSp(4,3) orbits of size 51,840, proving at least 3,265,920 global U6 singleton errors and singleton syndromes.
